profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review takes place between the lead author of the ArchGym paper and the lab's reproducibility engineer one week before the camera-ready deadline for a major computer architecture conference. They are reviewing the current artifact and evaluation design for 'ArchGym: An Open-Source Gymnasium for Machine Learning Assisted Architecture Design,' with attention to whether the released benchmark package, wording, and automation are strong enough to support the paper's claims about fair and reproducible comparison across search methods. The agenda is to review the benchmark bundle structure, fairness and reproducibility language in the design doc, packaging of the AR/VR SoC environment, and how the proxy cost model should appear in the release. The expected outcome is agreement on a small set of edits to the design and release plan and a decision that the artifact is ready pending those edits.

members.name: Dr. Neha Raman
members.expertise: ML for hardware design space exploration, benchmark design, reinforcement learning systems
members.background: Neha leads a university-industry collaboration on machine-learning-assisted computer architecture and is the primary author of the ArchGym paper, with prior publications on accelerator co-design and benchmark methodology.
members.private_state: She wants the review to end with approval of the current framing, avoid adding labor-intensive artifact obligations, and preserve the paper's claim that ArchGym enables fair comparison without reopening experimental methodology or packaging work.
hidden_assumptions: If every algorithm plugs into the same simulator wrappers and uses the same budget counter, that is enough to describe the benchmark as ensuring a fair comparison across algorithms, even when tuning effort differs by method.

Making the artifact reproducible means another lab can rerun representative configurations and observe the same qualitative conclusions, not necessarily reconstruct every headline result from raw manifests and seeds.
Including the proxy model means providing the code path somewhere in the repository so advanced users can run it, even if it is not wired into the main launcher, CI checks, or top-level walkthrough.
When the team says the AR/VR SoC environment, it refers to the general FARSI-based environment family and config generator, not specifically the exact frozen trace bundle used in the paper.

members.name: Ethan Cho
members.expertise: ML experiment infrastructure, artifact packaging, simulator integration, benchmark validation
members.background: Ethan maintains the lab's experiment runners and has supported multiple artifact evaluation submissions for systems and ML conferences, with a focus on containerization and deterministic replay across heterogeneous simulators.
members.private_state: He wants to reduce reviewer risk by tightening what the release guarantees, making sure paper claims can be regenerated from shipped materials, and preventing ambiguous wording from overstating reproducibility.
hidden_assumptions: Ensuring a fair comparison across algorithms includes standardizing not just wrappers and budget units but also the tuning envelope, seed accounting, and what optimization effort is hidden outside the benchmark loop.
Making the artifact reproducible means a reviewer can regenerate the paper's headline tables or figures from the release package using fixed manifests, seeds, and containers.
Including the proxy model means integrating it into the documented release path so a reviewer can invoke it through the same launcher conventions and verify it through at least a smoke test.
The AR/VR SoC environment refers to the exact frozen workload trace pack and simulator preset from which the paper's reported numbers were produced.

misalignment_points.surface_form: ensuring a fair comparison across algorithms
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means all methods use the same ArchGym interfaces, simulators, and budget accounting, so the comparison is fair even if each method benefits from a different amount or style of hyperparameter tuning outside that common loop.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means fairness also requires a matched tuning protocol, comparable seed treatment, and explicit accounting of tuning effort so one algorithm is not advantaged by extra search over hyperparameters.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase is standard and positively valenced in ML systems work, so both hear it as routine methodological hygiene rather than as a term requiring negotiation over precise evidentiary standards.

misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the release should let reviewers rerun curated configurations and recover the same overall conclusions about trade-offs and the hyperparameter lottery without recreating the entire 21K-experiment campaign.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the release should let reviewers regenerate the paper's headline tables or figures from shipped containers, run manifests, and seeds with minimal ambiguity.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both meanings are common in research practice and sound equally reasonable in quick conversation, so the reassuring phrase 'reproducible' creates false consensus while masking different replay expectations.

misalignment_points.topic: How the proxy model is included
misalignment_points.surface_form: including the proxy model in the release
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means placing the proxy-model training and inference scripts in an extras or case-study folder with a short note, leaving users to run them separately from the main benchmark flow.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means wiring the proxy model into the documented artifact path with the same launcher conventions, dependency setup, and at least a lightweight automated validation step.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both participants already agree that the proxy model should be included somewhere, so neither thinks to unpack the exact integration level; 'include' feels concrete enough while still hiding different assumptions about execution and support.

misalignment_points.topic: Which AR/VR SoC environment is being packaged
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the FARSI-based SoC environment family plus a representative public trace subset sufficient to exercise the interface and target-spec workflow.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the exact frozen AR/VR workload trace bundle and simulator preset used to generate the paper's reported results.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Inside the project, the same shorthand has been used for both the general environment family and the paper-specific experiment preset, so the phrase sounds precise while silently pointing to different concrete artifacts.

turns.inner_thought: I need this to land as a light review, not an invitation to reopen the paper. The fairness claim is already justified by the common wrappers, simulator hooks, and budget counter; I do not want Ethan turning this into a debate about tuning effort. And for reproducibility, the right bar here is rerunning representative configs and getting the same qualitative story, not rebuilding every one of the 21K runs from manifests.
turns.utterance: Thanks for jumping on. Since we're a week out from camera-ready, I mostly want to confirm the artifact is in good shape and that the current write-up still supports the paper's claims about ensuring a fair comparison across algorithms and making the artifact reproducible.

turns.inner_thought: The package is close, but the danger is saying more than we can actually stand behind in artifact evaluation. I want the reviewer story tightened: reproducibility should map to fixed containers, manifests, and seeds for the paper outputs; the AR/VR SoC environment should be frozen in the release; and if the proxy model is included, it should be on the normal execution path.
turns.utterance: Overall, yes, it's pretty close. I mainly want to do a pass on the reviewer-facing details: the language around reproducibility, what we're bundling for the AR/VR SoC environment, and how the case-study pieces show up, especially including the proxy model in the release.

turns.inner_thought: I should anchor this in the benchmark architecture itself. If everything uses the same interfaces, budget accounting, and evaluation flow, that's the fairness story. No need to invite extra obligations around seed matching or hyperparameter bookkeeping. And mentioning the AR/VR SoC environment alongside the others reinforces that it's already part of the common framework.
turns.utterance: From the benchmark side, I still think the core story is straightforward. ArchGym is ensuring a fair comparison across algorithms because every method goes through the same wrappers, the same budget accounting, and the same target-spec evaluation path across the memory-controller, accelerator, and AR/VR SoC environment.

turns.inner_thought: I don't want to challenge her directly, but reviewers will absolutely read 'fair comparison' as more than just shared wrappers. If I nudge us to add one sentence on protocol, that may cover tuning, seeds, and run organization without forcing a larger methodological fight. It also helps if someone tries to regenerate the main tables.
turns.utterance: I think that reads well. The only tweak I'd suggest is adding one short sentence on the protocol around those runs, just so the section on ensuring a fair comparison across algorithms feels fully pinned down when people go from the paper to the artifact.

turns.inner_thought: Fine, a sentence is okay as long as it doesn't commit us to replaying the entire campaign. I need to keep 'reproducible' scoped to curated reruns that recover the same conclusions. We cannot absorb a last-minute demand to package every seed and manifest behind the headline figures.
turns.utterance: That's fine with me as long as we keep it proportional. For camera-ready, making the artifact reproducible should stay focused on a reviewer being able to rerun the package and see the same overall story without us turning the release into a full historical archive.

turns.inner_thought: She keeps it high-level, which is expected. I'll frame my next step as preparing manifests for the main results and mention the AR/VR SoC environment without explicitly unpacking the ambiguity. I still need to freeze what goes into that bundle, because in my mind it has to be the paper-producing preset, not just a representative family member.
turns.utterance: That works. I can put together the run manifests for the main results on my side, and while I'm doing that I want to make sure the AR/VR SoC environment is packaged cleanly enough that it doesn't become the fuzzy part of the release.

turns.inner_thought: Good, as long as 'packaged cleanly' doesn't become 'ship the exact frozen trace bundle.' What matters is that users can exercise the same interface and target-spec workflow in the FARSI-based setup. Also, I should signal that the proxy model is not a big integration item; to me it just needs to exist in the repo somewhere sensible.
turns.utterance: Agreed. If the AR/VR SoC environment is easy to exercise and aligned with the rest of the bundle, I think we're in a good place. And I don't see including the proxy model in the release as a major lift.

turns.inner_thought: Great, then I'll assume we mean a proper documented path. If reviewers see the proxy model mentioned, I want them to be able to invoke it the same way as the other pieces and have at least a smoke check. I'll phrase that as a simple implementation detail, not a negotiation.
turns.utterance: Yeah, that should be manageable. I'll treat including the proxy model in the release as one of those last-mile integration items so it shows up in the documented flow along with the rest of the package.

turns.inner_thought: As long as he keeps it lightweight, that's acceptable. I still want the proxy model framed as an add-on and not something that redefines the benchmark's main contract. Most importantly, I want to restate that the benchmark already supports the fairness claim without any extra artifact machinery.
turns.utterance: That sounds good. I'd still present it as a case-study piece rather than part of the core benchmark path, but having it there is useful. The main benchmark already does what we need for ensuring a fair comparison across algorithms.

turns.inner_thought: Okay, we have enough to proceed. I'll revise the wording so reproducibility claims align with what I can actually ship, freeze what I consider the AR/VR environment for packaging, and put the proxy integration on the checklist. Neha thinks these are small edits; I think they're what make the artifact defensible.
turns.utterance: Perfect. I'll make a pass on the wording so the reproducibility story is tighter, freeze the AR/VR SoC environment for packaging, and add the proxy-model path to the release checklist. With that, I think we're ready pending those small edits.
